nextAblation: Compare always-admit fixed4096 slots against current always-admit growth, holding weak retention, source IDs/masks, ownership and all input/JVM/consumption settings equal. Verify unchanged exposure/hit outcomes and normal AUTO routes; this isolates cumulative-history growth from reopening admission. No runtime gain is assumed.
scopeFindings: All nine primary latency comparisons contain paired JVM ratios on both sides of one; none is a uniform six-pair latency improvement.
Late initial/ordinary reverses direction between prespecified median-based and mean-based paired estimators.
Ratios are medians of six paired process ratios; they are not ratios of the separate arm summaries. Five query measurements in each JVM are nested observations, not independent replications.
Always admission restores late-phase reuse but does not demonstrate an end-to-end latency win. Four resizes and larger reservation are observed; the latency cause is not isolated.

First-row timing includes upstream ordered result production and ends before consuming the first row lexical values. Current-query late-phase growth cannot directly account for this early interval under qualified rowwise demand. Cross-query heap/JIT history remains possible.

Allocation is usually stable within a JVM but differs by millions of bytes among JVMs with identical observable route/memo traces. Most measured allocation is on the query thread. JIT/escape-analysis sensitivity is a hypothesis, not measured evidence.

Hot-to-unique has no hits in its unique tail and grows twice after its admitted hot prefix. Its measured latency is not a demonstrated CPU regression; all arms and all five measurements remain included.

GC summaries cover complete JVM setup, warmups and measurements. Concurrent-cycle time overlaps execution and is not additive to pause time. Zero collectedMisses is expected under ordered-wrapper retention and does not establish weak rematerialization.
Ledger peaks are process-authority accounting during serial query windows, including estimated memo metadata and resize overlap. They are neither a separate query-ledger peak nor total retained heap.
The native route is ordered-factorized AUTO with no IR execution; the five measured queries are the qualified inner-source alternative-learning phase. Correctness tests cover other tiers separately.
